# package trace

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-modbus-trace/trace"
```

Package trace is the facade of go-modbus-trace: it opens a packet trace (pcap or pcapng, plain or gzip, from a file or a stream), finds the Modbus/TCP traffic in it and reports what it found.

The library is offline: it never opens a socket and never captures live. Its only clock is the trace's timestamps, and the same input gives the same output.

## Functions

### func Scan

```go
func Scan(ctx context.Context, f *File, o ScanOptions) (*FileSummary, []Flow, error)
```

Scan reads the whole trace once and returns its summary and its TCP flows with their Modbus assessment, ordered by flow ID. It frames MBAP in both directions but does not pair or decode PDUs.

A damaged file ends the scan with the results so far and an error wrapping ErrCorrupt. Cancelling ctx stops it between packets.

### func Walk

```go
func Walk(ctx context.Context, f *File, o ScanOptions, fn func(p *RawPacket) error) error
```

Walk reads every packet of the trace once and tells fn which TCP connection each belongs to (connection IDs are the same as Scan's). It does not reassemble or frame; a sub-trace extractor uses it.

Packets come in file order, with one exception: the IP fragments of a datagram are held until the fragment that completes it, and then given to fn, with the datagram's connection, just before it. Fragments of a datagram that never completes (or that the fragment budget dropped) come at the end of their file (or earlier, when the fragment budget lets them go) with Conn 0.

### type File

```go
type File struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

File is an opened trace: one or more paths (any number of passes), or a stream (one). Several paths are one continuous trace, read in the order given: connection state carries from one file to the next (rotated tcpdump -C/-G files).

#### func Open

```go
func Open(path string) (*File, error)
```

Open opens a trace file by path. Nothing is read until a pass runs.

#### func OpenFiles

```go
func OpenFiles(paths ...string) (*File, error)
```

OpenFiles opens several trace files that are one trace, in time order.

#### func OpenReader

```go
func OpenReader(r io.Reader) *File
```

OpenReader wraps a stream (for example standard input). It can be read by one pass only.

#### func (File) Frames

```go
func (f *File) Frames(refs []model.FrameRef) ([]Frame, error)
```

Frames re-reads the referenced packets of uncompressed trace files by their offsets, so an application can show raw bytes without keeping them. It is safe for concurrent use.

#### func (File) Name

```go
func (f *File) Name() string
```

Name returns the path ("-" for a stream); for several files the paths joined by commas.

#### func (File) Names

```go

```

Names returns the path of every input ("-" for a stream).

### type FileSummary

```go
type FileSummary struct {
	File        string      `json:"file"` // base name, or "-"; several joined by commas
	Format      string      `json:"format"`
	Gzip        bool        `json:"gzip"`
	InputBytes  int64       `json:"input_bytes"` // as stored (compressed for gzip)
	SHA256      string      `json:"sha256"`      // of the input as stored (empty for several: see Inputs); complete only if the read reached the end
	Inputs      []Input     `json:"inputs"`
	Packets     uint64      `json:"packets"`
	Bytes       uint64      `json:"bytes"` // captured bytes
	First       *time.Time  `json:"first,omitempty"`
	Last        *time.Time  `json:"last,omitempty"`
	Interfaces  []Interface `json:"interfaces"`
	Sections    []Section   `json:"sections,omitempty"`
	Snaplen     Snaplen     `json:"snaplen"`
	CaptureDrop *uint64     `json:"capture_drops,omitempty"` // sum of pcapng isb_ifdrop
	// Unsupported counts packets that did not yield a TCP segment, by
	// reason (not_ip, not_tcp, tunnel, ipsec, short, bad_header, ...).
	Unsupported map[string]uint64 `json:"unsupported"`
	Fragments   Fragments         `json:"fragments"`
	Reader      ReaderCounters    `json:"reader"`
	Connections ConnCounters      `json:"connections"`
	Quality     Quality           `json:"quality"`
	// TimeBackwards counts packets stamped earlier than the packet before
	// them (merged captures, clock steps). The pipeline never sorts.
	TimeBackwards uint64 `json:"time_backwards"`
	// TSOSegments counts IPv4 packets whose total length was 0: captured
	// on the sending host before TCP segmentation offload filled it in.
	// They are used at their captured length, as Wireshark does; not an
	// error.
	TSOSegments uint64 `json:"tso_segments"`
	// InternalErrors are recovered panics, the first 100 of
	// InternalErrorCount; a non-zero count is a bug worth reporting.
	InternalErrors     []InternalError `json:"internal_errors,omitempty"`
	InternalErrorCount uint64          `json:"internal_error_count,omitempty"`
	// Error is set when the read ended early on a damaged file.
	Error string `json:"error,omitempty"`
	// Transactions and TransactionFlags count the transactions by status
	// and by quality flag (Analyze only).
	Transactions     map[string]uint64 `json:"transactions,omitempty"`
	TransactionFlags map[string]uint64 `json:"transaction_flags,omitempty"`
}
```

FileSummary describes a trace (the result of Scan). With several input files the top-level file, format and size describe them together and Inputs each one.

#### func Analyze

```go
func Analyze(ctx context.Context, f *File, o Options, sink Sink) (*FileSummary, error)
```

Analyze reads the whole trace once and sends its events to sink: connections, transactions (paired, decoded and validated), gaps, resyncs and notes, in order of determination. Consumers sort transactions by their request time. It returns the file summary, with the transaction counters.

### type Options

```go
type Options struct {
	ScanOptions
	// Flows restricts the events to these flow IDs (as Scan numbers them);
	// nil means every flow.
	Flows []uint32
	// Slow is the latency above which a transaction is flagged slow (1 s).
	Slow time.Duration
	// MaxOutstanding bounds the unanswered requests per connection (256).
	MaxOutstanding int
	// OmitPDU leaves the PDU bytes out of the events (they stay
	// recoverable through the frame references).
	OmitPDU bool
	// FirstPacket, if set, is called once with the time of the first
	// timestamped packet, before any event that follows it (for selections
	// relative to the start of the trace).
	FirstPacket func(time.Time)
}
```

### type Quality

```go
type Quality struct {
	Retransmitted      uint64 `json:"retransmitted"`       // segments already delivered, seen again; not transactions, see model.FlagRetransmitted
	OutOfOrder         uint64 `json:"out_of_order"`        // segments held until the bytes before them came
	OverlapConflicts   uint64 `json:"overlap_conflict"`    // retransmissions whose bytes differ (the first data wins)
	Keepalives         uint64 `json:"keepalives"`          // one-byte probes before the next expected byte
	SYNRetransmits     uint64 `json:"syn_retransmits"`     // repeated SYNs of one epoch
	Gaps               uint64 `json:"gaps"`                // holes in a direction's byte stream, of any cause
	GapBytes           uint64 `json:"gap_bytes"`           // bytes in those holes, where the sequence numbers tell
	ReassemblyOverflow uint64 `json:"reassembly_overflow"` // gaps declared by Limits.BufferPerDir
	ReassemblyBudget   uint64 `json:"reassembly_budget"`   // gaps declared by Limits.BufferTotal
	Resyncs            uint64 `json:"resyncs"`             // framing resynchronisations
	ResyncFailed       uint64 `json:"resync_failed"`       // resyncs that found no header within Limits.ResyncScan
	JunkBytes          uint64 `json:"junk_bytes"`          // bytes of TCP payload that framed as nothing
	ForeignFrames      uint64 `json:"foreign_protocol"`
	SnaplenTruncated   uint64 `json:"snaplen_truncated"` // ADUs cut by the snap length
}
```

Quality counts TCP and framing conditions over the trace.

### type RawPacket

```go
type RawPacket struct {
	Part    int       // input file
	Frame   uint64    // 1-based within its file
	Iface   Interface // the capture interface (ID within its file)
	TimeNS  int64     // packet time, nanoseconds since 1970
	HasTime bool      // false for pcapng simple packets (TimeNS is then 0)
	OrigLen uint32    // length on the wire
	Data    []byte    // the captured bytes
	// Conn is the TCP connection the packet belongs to (as Scan numbers
	// them), 0 for anything else; Endpoints are its two ends.
	Conn      uint32
	Endpoints [2]netip.AddrPort
}
```

RawPacket is one captured packet, as Walk sees it. Data is valid only during the callback.
